reason: The digestive tube has a named slot for the salivary glands, whose ducts open into the mouth.
expectation: The salivary glands will fit into the digestive tube.

effect: The salivary glands are fitted; the pancreas and liver remain visible slots.
reason: The pancreas has a named slot and its duct leads to the small intestine.
expectation: The pancreas will fit into the digestive tube.

effect: The pancreas is fitted; the liver and gallbladder slot remains.
reason: The liver and gallbladder match the next named slot, with ducts leading toward the intestine.
expectation: The liver and gallbladder will fit into the digestive tube.

effect: The three glandular organs are fitted, completing the first goal; the meal still needs digestion.
reason: Salivary amylase is shown beside starch chains and begins starch digestion.
expectation: The amylase will begin breaking down the starch.

effect: Salivary amylase shortened the starch chains; further digestion is needed.
reaction: That matched the expected first stage.
reason: The pancreatic and intestinal starch-digesting enzymes are the visible next step for the shorter chains.
expectation: The enzymes will break the chains into smaller sugars suitable for absorption.

effect: The starch has been broken down into individual glucose molecules, leaving the other meal components to digest.
reaction: The two-stage starch breakdown was clear.
reason: Protein-digesting enzymes are shown acting on protein chains from food.
expectation: The enzymes will break the protein into smaller absorbable components.

effect: Protein digestion produced meal amino acids; fat remains to be broken down.
reason: Bile and lipase are shown working on dietary fat droplets.
expectation: Bile will help disperse the fat, and lipase will break it into smaller absorbable products.

effect: Fat digestion produced fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the remaining goal; bile disperses fat rather than acting as an enzyme.
reaction: The distinction between bile and lipase was useful and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking starch down in two stages was worthwhile: the planned pictures trace it from chains to individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining.

leastWorthwhile.text: The three named organ fittings were predictable and repetitive, although their ducts made the choices clear.

surprise.text: The final result clarified that bile disperses fat but is not an enzyme; lipase breaks the fat molecules apart.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the portal-vessel slot remained unfilled without an explanation in this chapter.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how glucose, amino acids and fat products cross the intestinal lining and reach the body, since this chapter stops after digestion.
